headline: World shares tumble as Iran war pushes crude prices over $110 a barrel
summary: World shares fell on Monday, with Japan's Nikkei 225 down more than 5%, after oil prices spiked near $120 a barrel. The sell-off followed the escalation of the Iran war.
why: The Nikkei 225 is Japan's benchmark stock index, and Japan imports most of its crude, so oil price spikes weigh heavily on its market.

impacts.name: Nikkei 225
impacts.why: Japan's benchmark index fell more than 5% as oil price spikes raised costs for an energy-importing economy.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The Iran war pushed crude oil above $110 a barrel, with prices spiking near $120. Higher energy costs hit investor sentiment across world equity markets.
